title: The Questions of King Milinda
attributionNote: The dialogue is anonymous. It presents questions put by the Indo-Greek king Menander (Milinda) to the monk Nāgasena; the king is a historical figure, the monk may be a literary creation.
description: The Questions of King Milinda is the longest and most philosophical of the paracanonical Pali books: a dialogue in which the Greek king Menander tests the monk Nāgasena on the self, rebirth, karma, the nature of the Buddha, and the practice of the path, using the famous simile of the chariot to show that a person is a convenient designation rather than a substance. It is a bridge between Greek and Buddhist thought.
historicalContext: The Milindapañha survives in Pali, with a Chinese recension and a Sanskrit parallel; it is canonical in the Burmese tradition but excluded from the Sinhalese canon. T. W. Rhys Davids translated it in two volumes for the Sacred Books of the East (volumes 35 and 36, 1890 and 1894).
availabilityNote: Complete. Both Sacred Books of the East volumes (35 and 36) are combined here and streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one chapter per page. Chapter labels carry the source volume because the printed numbering restarts between them. The introductions, addenda and indexes are not part of the work.
